section_summary: This section contains correspondence about disputed Japanese trademark applications, including proposed registrations of “Underwood,” “television,” “PURE,” and “GTD.” It also includes American Embassy lists of Japanese trademark applications published in 1941 and an extended file on Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation’s appeal against the rejection of its GTD mark.

people.name: J. A. Bertsch
people.role: Consulting chemical engineer and letter writer

people.name: Joseph W. Ballantine
people.role: Acting Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Henry C. Hawkins
people.role: Chief, Division of Commercial Treaties and Agreements

people.name: F. H. Payne
people.role: Chairman of the Board, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation

people.name: Maxwell M. Hamilton
people.role: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Susumu Nakagawa
people.role: Holder of Japanese GTD trademark registration

people.name: F. A. Smith
people.role: General Manager, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation

people.name: I. Inoue
people.role: Attorney in Japanese trademark invalidation proceeding

subfiles.title: Telegram asking for reply to cosmetic company letter
subfiles.about: The company asks for a wire reply to its December 27 letter.
subfiles.summary: Requests a reply by telegram at the company’s expense.

subfiles.title: Reply to M. Stein Cosmetic Co.
subfiles.about: The Department says its reply is being mailed.
subfiles.summary: Advises that a reply is being mailed that day.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on allegedly Japanese barber chair marketed as American
subfiles.about: A complaint from Alexandria, Egypt, concerns the origin claimed for a barber chair.
subfiles.summary: Points to another file containing the complaint and a request for consular investigation.

subfiles.title: Underwood typewriter trademark application in Japan
subfiles.from: George A. Atkinson, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports T. Takemori’s application for an Underwood remanufacturing mark.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy doubts that Takemori is an authorized Underwood rebuilder and urges notice to the American company. Opposition must reach the Japanese Patent Office before August 10, 1940.

subfiles.title: Sketch of Underwood mark
subfiles.about: The attachment depicts the proposed Underwood mark.
subfiles.summary: Sketch bearing the words “Master Underwood.”

subfiles.title: Notice to Underwood Elliot Fisher Company
subfiles.from: Ralph W. S. Hill, Acting Legal Adviser
subfiles.about: The Department forwards the Japanese application and its opposition deadline.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Embassy despatch and trademark sketch and alerts the company that any protest must be filed in Tokyo before August 10, 1940.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese royalty payments
subfiles.about: Bertsch asks how to secure dollar payments under a prospective Japanese chemical process license.
subfiles.summary: Seeks guidance on receiving at least 80 percent of royalties in U.S. dollars.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese exchange permits and royalties
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains the uncertainty of remitting royalties from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Japanese authorities control exchange permits, and even a good-faith royalty contract gives no assurance that funds can be remitted to the United States.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser routing note
subfiles.about: A handwritten note suggests sending a form or copy to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Brief, partly illegible instruction mentioning Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department letter on “television” trademark
subfiles.from: James L. Brown, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Commerce reports Ukichi Murakami’s Japanese application for the word “television.”
subfiles.summary: Citing concerns from American radio manufacturers, Commerce asks State to pursue denial of the proposed registration.

subfiles.title: Instruction to oppose “television” registration
subfiles.about: The Department requests Japanese rejection or cancellation of the “television” mark.
subfiles.summary: Argues that “television” is generic and descriptive, citing the Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser memorandum on “television”
subfiles.about: The memorandum proposes asking Japanese authorities to reject or cancel the “television” mark.
subfiles.summary: It supplies the argument that “television” is a common descriptive word and quotes treaty provisions on marks lacking distinctive character.

subfiles.title: Japanese trade mark applications published June 12, 1941
subfiles.from: Donald W. Lamm, American Vice Consul
subfiles.about: The Embassy lists Japanese applications published in the Trade Mark Journal.
subfiles.summary: The report identifies proposed marks, goods classes, and applicants across medicines, paints, textiles, foods, paper, and other products. It states that opposition must be filed within 60 days of publication.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting missing Commerce letter on “television”
subfiles.about: Grew reports that the Commerce letter mentioned in the June instruction was missing.
subfiles.summary: Requests instructions because the referenced enclosure was not received.

subfiles.title: Corrected copy of Grew’s “television” telegram
subfiles.about: The corrected telegram confirms nonreceipt of the Commerce letter.
subfiles.summary: Corrects the earlier copy to say the letter “has not been received.”

subfiles.title: Japanese trade mark applications of July 31, 1941
subfiles.from: Donald W. Lamm, American Vice Consul
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports Japanese trademark applications listed on July 31.
subfiles.summary: Lists proposed marks, applicants, and goods classes, including chemicals, silk, flour, matches, and incense.

subfiles.title: Japanese trade mark applications of August 7, 1941
subfiles.from: Donald W. Lamm, American Vice Consul
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports Japanese trademark applications listed on August 7.
subfiles.summary: The report records marks, goods classes, and applicants for medicines, cosmetics, machinery, food, stationery, oils, and miscellaneous merchandise. It notes the opposition period following publication.

subfiles.title: Japanese trade mark applications of August 14, 1941
subfiles.from: Donald W. Lamm, American Vice Consul
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports Japanese trademark applications listed on August 14.
subfiles.summary: The lengthy list identifies many proposed medicinal marks alongside applications for machinery, vehicles, paints, stationery, and other goods. It provides applicants and classes for possible review or opposition.

subfiles.title: Japanese trade mark applications of August 21, 1941
subfiles.from: Donald W. Lamm, American Vice Consul
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports Japanese trademark applications listed on August 21.
subfiles.summary: Lists applicants and classes for marks covering matches, medicines, paints, soaps, transport equipment, paper, food, and other goods.

subfiles.title: Commercial Treaties and Agreements handwritten note
subfiles.from: Division of Commercial Treaties and Agreements
subfiles.about: A largely illegible handwritten note concerns handling a trade mark matter.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten routing note; substantive wording is unclear.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs handwritten note
subfiles.about: A largely illegible handwritten note appears to concern a reply.
subfiles.summary: Brief handwritten note with mostly unreadable text.

subfiles.title: Borden Company protest against “PURE” mark
subfiles.about: Borden asks State to oppose Japanese registration of “PURE” for dairy products.
subfiles.summary: Borden argues that the word is descriptive and lacks the distinctiveness required by Japanese law. It requests urgent representations before registration, despite expiration of the statutory opposition period.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Borden
subfiles.about: The Department responds to Borden’s objection to the “PURE” application.
subfiles.summary: Agrees with Borden’s views and says the Embassy in Tokyo will be asked to make representations.

subfiles.title: Borden request for updates on “PURE”
subfiles.from: Arthur C. Mac Mahon, The Borden Company
subfiles.to: Department of State, attention Green H. Hackworth
subfiles.about: Borden asks to be told the result of Embassy representations on “PURE.”
subfiles.summary: Thanks the Department for its November 27 letter and requests updates.

subfiles.title: Instruction to investigate and oppose “PURE” registration
subfiles.about: The Department authorizes action against the Japanese “PURE” dairy trademark.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is to investigate the application and seek rejection or cancellation if it remains viable. The Department cites the descriptive meaning of “pure,” Japanese law, and the industrial property convention.

subfiles.title: Counselor’s referral of Greenfield complaint
subfiles.about: Moore refers a former War Department official’s letter for reply.
subfiles.summary: Asks Hamilton to answer Payne’s attached letter.

subfiles.title: Greenfield complaint over GTD refusal
subfiles.from: F. H. Payne, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield asks State for help after Japan rejects its GTD panel mark.
subfiles.summary: Payne says Greenfield’s Japanese GTD registrations from 1921 and 1925 predate the 1930 mark cited against its new Class 17 application. He encloses the attorneys’ account of the refusal and asks for assistance.

subfiles.title: Moore’s acknowledgment to Payne
subfiles.about: Moore refers Greenfield’s trademark complaint to Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Promises direct contact from the division and cautions that resolution may be difficult.

subfiles.title: Ward memorandum revising proposed Greenfield reply
subfiles.about: Ward proposes language addressing Greenfield’s appeal and possible diplomatic representations.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum notes the February 5, 1939 appeal deadline and the need to exhaust Japanese remedies. It says the refusal appears to disregard Greenfield’s earlier rights and offers Embassy discussion if requested.

subfiles.title: Department letter offering assistance to Greenfield
subfiles.about: The Department discusses Greenfield’s appeal rights and possible Embassy intervention.
subfiles.summary: It advises that an appeal is likely necessary before formal diplomatic representations. If Greenfield wishes, the Ambassador may discuss the refusal with Japanese officials; supporting mark descriptions and legal arguments would help.

subfiles.title: Greenfield requests Embassy intervention
subfiles.from: F. H. Payne, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield says it will appeal and requests discussion with Japanese authorities.
subfiles.summary: Payne encloses trademark images and attorneys’ arguments for forwarding to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from Greenfield attorneys’ May 3 letter
subfiles.about: The attorneys argue that Greenfield’s older GTD marks should defeat the cited 1930 registration.
subfiles.summary: They contend that the Japanese examiner should apply a consistent treatment of the marks.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Greenfield appeal decision
subfiles.about: Hamilton confirms instructions to Ambassador Grew about the GTD case.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the planned appeal and says the enclosures will be sent to Grew.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Grew on Greenfield GTD case
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department asks Grew to seek reversal of the Japanese Patent Bureau’s GTD refusal.
subfiles.summary: The instruction recounts Greenfield’s earlier registrations, the rejection of its new mark, and its decision to appeal. Grew is asked to discuss the matter with appropriate Japanese authorities using enclosed correspondence.

subfiles.title: Edwards, Bower & Pool legal explanation of GTD refusal
subfiles.about: Greenfield’s lawyers explain why the cited Nakagawa mark should not bar its application.
subfiles.summary: The firm supplies correspondence and compares Greenfield’s 1921 and 1925 Class 17 registrations with Nakagawa’s 1930 mark. It argues that the goods do not justify giving Nakagawa’s registration such broad blocking effect.

subfiles.title: Notice that GTD appeal was filed
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: The firm reports that its Japanese associate filed the GTD appeal.
subfiles.summary: Confirms appeal filing and promises further news.

subfiles.title: Greenfield forwards State Department letter
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield forwards Hamilton’s letter to its lawyers.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Department’s reply about Embassy assistance.

subfiles.title: Copy of Hamilton’s reply to Payne
subfiles.about: Hamilton confirms the Department’s action on Greenfield’s request.
subfiles.summary: States that Ambassador Grew is being instructed and the supporting documents forwarded.

subfiles.title: Langner firm on GTD appeal coordination
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: The firms coordinate Japanese counsel and supporting decisions for the GTD appeal.
subfiles.summary: Logan plans to provide registration lists and the favorable CTP invalidation decision to the Japanese associate. He also expects State Department involvement.

subfiles.title: Edwards firm proceeds with GTD appeal
subfiles.about: The attorneys report progress on Greenfield’s Japanese appeal.
subfiles.summary: They are proceeding with the appeal and seeking comments from Asamura and Higuchi.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese counsel’s comments
subfiles.about: The attorneys request comments on Greenfield’s GTD appeal.
subfiles.summary: Encloses recent correspondence and asks Japanese counsel for suggestions.

subfiles.title: Supporting material sent for GTD appeal
subfiles.about: The attorneys send a chronology and favorable CTP decision for the GTD appeal.
subfiles.summary: Encloses trademark lists, correspondence, and the Japanese Patent Office’s CTP invalidation decision.

subfiles.title: List of Greenfield Japanese GTD trademarks
subfiles.about: The schedule catalogs Greenfield’s Japanese GTD registrations and pending applications.
subfiles.summary: Lists marks and classes dating from 1917, including the rejected Class 17 application.

subfiles.title: Japanese decision invalidating CTP mark
subfiles.to: Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation and opposing party
subfiles.about: The Patent Office invalidates a CTP mark confusingly similar to Greenfield’s GTD device.
subfiles.summary: The judges find that the marks’ overall appearance and related goods could confuse purchasers about origin. The translated decision invalidates registration No. 255,570.

subfiles.title: Langner firm instructs GTD appeal
subfiles.from: F. H. Logan, Langner, Parry, Card & Langner
subfiles.about: The firm directs its Japanese associate to appeal rejection of Greenfield’s GTD application.
subfiles.summary: Reports that an appeal memorandum has been prepared, while cautioning that success is uncertain.

subfiles.title: Greenfield instructs attorneys to appeal
subfiles.from: F. A. Smith, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield authorizes an appeal before the February 5, 1939 deadline.
subfiles.summary: Smith also says Greenfield will ask State to have the Ambassador raise the case in Tokyo.
